title: No Redundancy, No Stall: Lightweight Streaming 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-time Rendering
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering incurs redundant computations and memory stalls affecting real-time performance.
motivation: Efficient 3D Gaussian Splatting acceleration enables practical real-time rendering in resource-constrained environments.
method: Algorithm-hardware co-design reducing computational redundancy through viewpoint transformation. Workload-aware accelerator design. Streaming architecture eliminating memory stalls.
key_novelty: First algorithm-hardware co-optimized approach for 3D Gaussian Splatting with redundancy elimination and stall prevention.
limitations: Comparison to existing 3D rendering accelerators not provided; applicability to different 3D rendering techniques unclear.
